# Unexpected inconsistent behaviour when using 'model_construct'

### Description

I came across something unexpected / inconstistent when passing extra values to `model_construct`.

```
class A(BaseModel):
    attribute: int

a = A.model_construct(another_attribute=":(")
```

In the documentation, it says:
> [...] Creates a new model setting __dict__ and __pydantic_fields_set__ from trusted or pre-validated data. Default values are respected, but no other validation is performed. Behaves as if Config.extra = 'allow' was set since it adds all passed values

When inspecting the created object, the attribute doesn't seem to be present:
```
a  # A()
a.model_dump()  # {}
a.model_extra  # None
```

Then, however, I discovered, that the attribute is indeed present and can (must) be accessed directly as it doesn't show up in the dump result:
```
a.another_attribute  # ':('
```

This is somehow unexpected, because I thought the attribute would also appear in the `repr` and `model_dump` result. 


What I found to be inconsistent is the following sentence:
> Behaves as if Config.extra = 'allow' was set since it adds all passed values

When I manually set `extra="allow"`, the extra values to `model_construct` show up as expected:
```
class B(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")
    attribute: int


b = B.model_construct(another_attribute=":)")

b  # B(another_attribute=':)')
b.another_attribute  # ':)'
b.model_dump()  # {'another_attribute': ':)'}
b.model_extra  # {'another_attribute': ':)'}
```

But this somehow contradicts the statement, that `model_construct` just behaves as if "Config.extra = 'allow' was set" as it actually takes into account the current configuration.

A notice of this behavior in the documentation would be nice.

### Example Code

```Python
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class A(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")  # ignore behaves the same

    attribute: int


a = A.model_construct(another_attribute=":(")

a  # A()
a.another_attribute  # ':('
a.model_dump()  # {}
a.model_extra  # None


class B(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")
    attribute: int


b = B.model_construct(another_attribute=":)")

b  # B(another_attribute=':)')
b.another_attribute  # ':)'
b.model_dump()  # {'another_attribute': ':)'}
b.model_extra  # {'another_attribute': ':)'}
```
